- When sentiment is positive (0.33) and model forecasts are high, reduce forecasted values by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.  
- After a recent spike in price, model tends to overshoot — cap forecasted peaks at 10–15% below the immediate prior high.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price has been trending downward, model often underestimates the drop — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day.  
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is low — apply a 1–3% downward bias for first 5–7 days.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day forecasts — if model is above 75% of recent 18-day average, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment is positive and model is below recent low, avoid aggressive upward correction — instead, align with 18-day moving average.
